title.value: DeepFT: Fault-Tolerant Edge Computing using a Self-Supervised Deep Surrogate Model
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly indicated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: DeepFT: Fault-Tolerant Edge Computing using a Self-Supervised Deep Surrogate Model

extractions.description: This paper discusses a fault-tolerance method for edge computing called DeepFT. It utilizes a self-supervised learning approach to predict and remediate faults in edge computing environments by using a deep surrogate model. This method is intended to overcome the limitations of traditional supervised learning by adapting to non-stationary workloads and enhancing reliability in edge computing.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper addresses optimization and fault tolerance in edge computing, its focus is not directly on Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development. The main goal is to improve fault tolerance and operational efficiency in computing, not sustainability or ecological impact.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Although a large amount of generated log data can be mined for fault prediction, labeling this data for training is a manual process and thus a limiting factor for automation. Due to this, many companies resort to unsupervised fault-tolerance models.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development but rather on improving fault tolerance in edge computing, which isn't directly related to sustainable development goals outlined.
primary_category.quote: The emergence of latency-critical AI applications has been supported by the evolution of the edge computing paradigm. However, edge solutions are typically resource-constrained, posing reliability challenges due to heightened contention for compute and communication capacities.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary theme is not related to sustainable development, there are no secondary categories applicable.
secondary_categories.quote: Challenges. The key challenge tackled in this paper is to devise a proactive overload and contention protection scheme that is efficient and accurate in the face of a lack of labeled training data.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category does not apply as the main focus of the paper is on technical advancements in fault-tolerance in edge computing, not on sustainability.
primary_sub_category.quote: DeepFT uses a deep surrogate model to accurately predict and diagnose faults in the system and co-simulation based self-supervised learning to dynamically adapt the model in volatile settings.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no sub-categories applicable since the focus is not related to climate or ecological challenges.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We aim to prevent over-utilization faults by adjusting the task scheduling and migration decisions.

applications.justification: The paper highlights the application of the DeepFT method specifically for enhancing fault tolerance in volatile edge computing environments.
applications.quote: To cope with this, we propose a novel modeling approach, called DeepFT, to proactively avoid system overloads and their adverse effects by optimizing the task scheduling and migration decisions.

new_primary_category.justification: The current categories sufficiently outline sustainable development goals, but this paper does not align with those goals directly.
new_primary_category.quote: Our contributions. In this work, we propose DeepFT1, a scalable Deep surrogate model based Fault-Tolerance method.
